Question: Do developers and hair color brands have to match? For example, I have Clairol Demi perm developer and Mystic Divine demi perm color.

Question: Why is shampoo first before conditioner?
Answer: Shampoos generally have a slightly higher pH than conditioners. This allows for gentle lifting of the cuticle to help remove oils and daily debris, along with styling products off the hair. Once the hair is shampoo and rinse thoroughly, the cuticle is still slightly raised. Conditioner has a lower pH. Normally from 3.5 to 4.0. It's job is to close down the cuticle and re-acidify the hair after shampooing. By closing down the cuticle, the hair will be shinier and not as difficult to detangle. Even fine here can benefit from a lightweight daily conditioning after shampooing.

Question: My hairdresser washed my hair right after curl perming my hair. She also blow dried my hair. Did she do the right thing? I don’t think she should’ve done those?

After the required processing time, the hair is rinsed thoroughly with the rod still in place. Towel blotted very well and a neutralizer is applied for approximately 5 minutes. After this time, the rods will be removed and the hair will be rinsed thoroughly. Shampoo is not part of the step. For longevity it is preferred the hair be rinsed thoroughly and if there's any type of conditioner added it will be something required by the manufacturer after the permanent wave is completed. Perms will hold up longer if they are allowed to dry naturally immediately after the service. You are not to shampoo your hair for a minimum of 72 hours, which makes me wonder why your hair with shampooed after your perm. The hair is under fragile state immediately after and I prefer not to use Heat until the 72-hour period is over. I am thinking that maybe the individual who did your perm, drop the rods and panic because they thought it was too curly. So in order to relax it a little bit this individual shampooed your hair, and used heat to style it. Or, they just don't have any sense and I see a lot of that in our industry. Perms have become trendy again and for many years it wasn't something styles for doing on a regular basis like they're starting to do again now.

Question: I had my hair bleached 6 months ago, and decided to go back with my natural color brunette that was in mid May is it safe to get a spiral perm?

If you put a permanent wave on top of the bleached hair you have an 80% chance of losing 80% of that bleached hair. If you find someone that is really knowledgeable and has a great deal of expertise in perming bleached hair, they will take the steps necessary to keep the hair from dissolving. With that being said, someone super ultra Savvy who is capable of doing this can give you two choices. A very mild perm that's going to relax considerably on the hair that's previously bleached. And the first three inches will hardly do anything at all. If a strong enough solution is used to perm the first three inches of hair, the rest of the hair will dissolve. I have permed bleach hair and I don't like to do it. I worked for a perm manufacturer for years and I am quite Savvy with most perm chemistries. The best thing you can do, is grow out all the bleached hair and cut it off before you even consider having a spiral perm.

Question: I used a level 5-6 toner on a level 7. Why didn’t it work?

And based on those underlying tones, what was the color of the level five or six toner used? Was it a level 5 toner or was it a level six toner? They work on what's known as the rate of absorption. Whatever is the color of the hair combines with whatever color you put on the hair. This is why we can take a light violet/ beige toner and put it on yellow blonde hair and get a light natural blonde versus a violet blonde. On the color wheel Violet is the opposite of yellow. And why the two combined together give a natural or what's known as neutral color. If someone truly wanted a violet color they would have to add more Violet to the formula to offset the rate of absorption with the existing yellow eating up the violet color applied to the hair. Question: How do I get extremely soft hair? My hair is super rough, dry, and low porosity.I tried many tips on Google that works well with low porosity hairs, it only works when my hair is wet, after that it goes back to super dry and rough.☹️

Question: There's a question I can't seem to get a straight answer on. Does using "baby shampoo" (let's use Johnson & Johnson formula) strip hair color from hair better than others or is it the safest gentlest on it? I was told it removes it like no other.

Question: Why is my hair not going back to my natural curl after straightening once and already washing it several times? I have curly hair and I straightened in January. Its May now, but my hair is still straight? How do I fix this?
Answer: People outside the hair industry never quite explain things well enough for us to figure it out. If you had your hair permanently straightened with chemicals, it is not going to come out until you cut it all out. You should have curly New Growth at the scalp and then an Abrupt start with the straight hair approximately 1 and 1/2 to 2 inches from the scalp.
